steps.title: What you are building
Gather the electronics and kit cables
Print the 21 new parts
Tools and consumables
Soldering and wire list
Check the neck and head servo IDs
Flash the UART bridge
Set the power jumper and trim the header tails
Solder the two UART wires into J12
Set the 5991 to 15 V and the two XL4015 to 7.40 V and 5.00 V
Open both hips so the torso base can go in
Check the cables already in each leg
Open the thigh (only on a leg missing a thigh plug)
Plug both thigh servos and slide them back
Plug the ankle servo (only if its plug is missing)
Close each leg and tie the leg cables
Plug the hip cable into the hip-roll motor
Stack the yaw links, rings, torso base and hip-yaw motors
Fasten each yaw link to its hip-yaw motor
Put the hip-roll motors back into the yaw links
Screw the BNO085 onto the pack rib on the bench
Slide in the rear electronics pack
Fasten the hip-yaw motors to the torso
Slide both legs back onto the hip-roll outputs
Plug the hip cables into ID5 and ID10
Mount the OpenRB-150 in the pack
Connect the 7 V pair and plug in the three links
Plug the leg links into ID5 and ID10
Plug the IMU cable
Fit the rear box frame with the four cover screws
Screw the 5991 into the bottom tier and loop its 15 V wires
Screw in the 5 V converter, then the 7 V converter above it, IN on the right
Lead the 7 V pair and the head 5 V lead to their converters' OUT blocks
Close the box with its cap lid
Seat the two neck motors
Fasten the neck cases and rear centres
Connect ID12 to ID11 (100 mm)
Prepare the yaw motor on the pitch bracket
Join the upper neck to ID11 and connect 11 → 13
Fit the bracket wire clip under its screw
Lower the neck into the open torso
Close the two torso shells, fit the torso wire clip and screw each shell to the pack
Seat ID15 in the jaw support and plug its cable
Check the lower head shell
Spring the jaw into the lower shell from below
Prepare the roll motor on the yaw fork
Drop the fork with ID14 into the shell
Set the head on ID13 and connect 13 → 14
Lower the jaw support with ID15 and screw it down
Fit the head wire clip under the fourth support screw
Screw the jaw to the ID15 horn
Fit the eye trim into the face panel and screw it from behind
Screw the camera to the back of the face
Set the face and camera on the head
Prepare the head cap
Seat the speaker in the cap collar with the retainer
Mount the amplifier on its two posts
Stick the Wi-Fi antenna inside the cap roof
Stick the five copper touch pads and the XIAO inside the cap
Mount the Radxa Cubie A7Z on the cap rails
Fit the cap wire clip under the fourth A7Z screw
Plug the antenna cable onto the A7Z
Plug the five amplifier wires onto the A7Z
Plug the four XIAO wires onto the A7Z
Check the plug on every wire that goes to the A7Z and flag it
Run the 8-wire bundle through the torso, bracket and head clips
Plug the bundle onto the A7Z, press it into the cap clip and lower the cap
Unpowered checks
Set up the A7Z software
First power: converter readback, bus scan, Shutdown 52 and voltage-limit check
Check the IMU, camera, Wi-Fi and speaker
Range-of-motion check with torque off
Measure the servo current through the OpenRB
Screw the head shut
Close the mouth and weigh the robot
Snap the switch into the backpack floor, rocker down
Clip the DFR1202 behind the front plate and lead its plugs out of the window
Swap the rear converter box for the battery backpack
Slide the battery in upright and connect plug 1
Close the backpack with its cap
